q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a kurta?
title: Kurta carbon footprint per piece
short: Take the fabric issued per kurta, including cutting waste, and multiply by the mill's per-metre figure. Add embroidery or printing, trims, stitching and pressing electricity and packing, then divide the unit's energy by kurtas passed.
audience: Ethnic wear makers and garment exporters, including Jaipur and Lucknow units

ul: Fabric per kurta from the marker, including waste and shrinkage allowance.
Hand block, screen or digital printing: dye, steam and dryer energy per metre.
Chikankari or machine embroidery: thread and machine hours.
Sewing machines, overlock machines and steam irons with their boiler.

p: Report per style and size band, since a long A-line kurta uses noticeably more fabric than a short straight one. Give the fabric and its weight in GSM.

example.title: Worked example: kurta unit per piece (one month)
lines: Plant total: 27,450 / 40,000 = 0.686 kg CO2 per kurta
Add fabric, printing and trims for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
